report.summary: Reviewed evolution.py chunk 1 of 1; enumerated 15 docstring/comment claims, 4 kept, 3 broken, 8 uncheckable; no files changed, no tests run.
risks: line 95 | high | asyncio.gather without per-task timeout in generate_candidates can hang forever despite DEFAULT_EVAL_TIMEOUT_S; docstring claim 'Wall-clock ceiling for ONE candidate's test run' does not cover generation | Add per-task timeout or document that generation is unbounded

line 110 | high | evaluate_candidates catches all exceptions from gather and logs 'Error evaluating candidates' but leaves candidate fields untouched; an unexpected exception during gather can leave candidates unscored with no error set | Inspect whether any path inside evaluate_single can raise outside its own try/except; if so, set candidate.error in the outer except

line 172 | medium | check_import_provenance result is trusted to have .ok and .as_error() attributes; if the function returns None or a different shape, AttributeError is raised and caught by the outer except, leaving all candidates unscored silently | Verify the return type of check_import_provenance in daedalus/eval/provenance.py

line 126 | medium | sys.executable -m pytest assumes the working directory is set to the candidate worktree; if the worktree has no pytest configuration or the command fails for environment reasons, the candidate is scored 0.0 without distinguishing test failure from environment failure | Inspect the ShadowShellManager to see how worktree_path is set and whether it is guaranteed to be a directory with a runnable pytest

line 174 | medium | The provenance check happens before process spawn but after candidate.completed check; if candidate.completed is set by a previous run and the worktree has since changed, the check may be stale | Inspect how candidate.completed and worktree_path are updated in ShadowShellManager
todos: Verify check_import_provenance return type and semantics in daedalus/eval/provenance.py
Confirm that ShadowShellManager.run_task returns CandidateBranch instances with worktree_path set
Consider adding a per-task timeout to generate_candidates to align with the timeout policy
Review whether the outer except in evaluate_candidates should set candidate.error for all candidates when an unexpected exception occurs

handoff.purpose: Review the EvolutionaryOrchestrator class: candidate generation, evaluation, and selection logic with docstring claims.

symbols.name: DEFAULT_EVAL_TIMEOUT_S
symbols.note: Wall-clock ceiling for one candidate's test run, set to 600.0 seconds.

symbols.name: EvolutionaryOrchestrator
symbols.note: Experimental candidate runner: generates isolated branches, runs configured test command, retains only passing candidates. Not autonomous evolution, not a promotion boundary.

symbols.name: EvolutionaryOrchestrator.__init__
symbols.note: Stores a factory callable that returns ShadowShellManager instances.

symbols.name: EvolutionaryOrchestrator.generate_candidates
symbols.note: Spawns N ShadowShellManager instances in parallel via asyncio.gather; returns only candidates that are CandidateBranch instances; logs exceptions.

symbols.name: EvolutionaryOrchestrator.evaluate_candidates
symbols.note: Evaluates candidates by running sys.executable -m pytest in each candidate's worktree; sets candidate.score and candidate.error; handles timeout and exceptions.

symbols.name: EvolutionaryOrchestrator.select_best
symbols.note: Selects the best candidate based on score; returns None if no candidate is completed, error-free, and score >= 100.0.

claims.text: Wall-clock ceiling for ONE candidate's test run. Without it a candidate that hangs ... blocks the whole `gather` below forever, and the run has no way to end.
claims.why: The timeout is applied in evaluate_candidates via asyncio.wait_for(process.communicate(), timeout=timeout_s), which caps each candidate's test run.

claims.text: Experimental candidate runner: generate isolated branches, run a configured test command, and retain only a passing candidate.
claims.why: The chunk implements branch generation and test running, but 'retain only a passing candidate' is not visible here; selection logic exists in select_best but 'retain' implies storage or return state not shown.

claims.text: This is not autonomous code evolution and it is not a promotion boundary. A trusted verifier still has to inspect a candidate before it can be merged into the primary workspace.
claims.why: The code does not autonomously evolve or promote; it only scores candidates. The claim about a trusted verifier and merge boundary is not observable in this chunk.

claims.text: Spawns N ShadowShellManager instances in parallel to attempt the task.
claims.why: The method creates one manager per population_size and calls run_task concurrently via asyncio.gather.
It runs pytest via asyncio.create_subprocess_exec and gathers the per-candidate tasks with asyncio.gather.
Every branch in evaluate_single sets candidate.score and candidate.error (or leaves them as-is for unexpected exceptions, but normal paths set them).

claims.text: THE INTERPRETER IS PART OF THE MEASUREMENT. This shells out to ``sys.executable -m pytest``, never to a bare ``pytest``, and the difference is not cosmetic -- it decides WHICH TREE gets scored.

MEASURED 2026-07-29, running the same test file two ways inside a worktree that shadows ``daedalus/``: bare `pytest` -> daedalus resolved to the PRIMARY checkout; `python -m pytest` -> daedalus resolved to the WORKTREE copy.
claims.why: The measurement is not reproducible from this code; it references external behavior of pytest and the editable install.

claims.text: The editable install pins ``daedalus`` to the primary checkout by absolute path via an ``_EditableFinder`` on ``sys.meta_path``. Bare ``pytest`` puts only each test file's own basedir on ``sys.path``, never the worktree root, so nothing shadows that finder and the candidate's edits are invisible to its own tests. ``-m`` puts the working directory on ``sys.path[0]``, ahead of ``PathFinder``, which is ahead of ``_EditableFinder`` -- so the candidate's code wins, as it must.
claims.why: This describes Python packaging internals not present in this chunk; cannot be verified from the code here.

claims.text: Until this changed, every score this class produced described the primary checkout's code running the candidate's tests.
claims.why: Historical claim; not verifiable from current code.

claims.text: This is still a BINARY, whole-suite signal and it is still not a promotion boundary -- see ``docs/adrs/015-ariadne-preconditions.md``.
claims.why: The chunk only sets score 100.0 or 0.0, so binary whole-suite is plausible, but 'not a promotion boundary' is a policy claim not observable in this code.

claims.text: The stronger measurement (``daedalus.eval.correctness.evaluate_change``, which freezes the selection before candidate code runs and reports five outcomes with precedence) is the intended replacement; this fix makes the interim signal describe the right tree, nothing more.
claims.why: References another module not present in this chunk.

claims.text: VERIFY the docstring's argument instead of trusting it. `-m` plus this cwd makes the candidate win by sys.path ORDERING, and nothing enforced that ordering still holds -- a set PYTHONPATH, a candidate whose daedalus/ was destroyed, or a future 'simplification' back to bare `pytest` all produce the same worst-shaped failure: tests pass, score is high, wrong tree. See daedalus.eval.provenance.
claims.why: The comment claims a verification mechanism exists, but the actual check_import_provenance function is external; the chunk only calls it and trusts its result.

claims.text: A failure here VOIDS THE EVALUATION and is not a candidate score. -1.0 is this module's own 'not evaluated' marker (used above for an incomplete candidate); 0.0 would mean 'measured, and bad', which would let an unrunnable evaluation argue against a candidate nobody actually judged.
claims.why: When provenance fails, the code sets score = -1.0 and error to the provenance error, and returns, so the evaluation is voided.

claims.text: A hung candidate is a FAILED candidate, never an unscored one left to block the gather. Kill it and say why.
claims.why: On TimeoutError, the code sets score = 0.0, sets error, kills the process, and logs.

observations.what: generate_candidates uses asyncio.gather without a per-task timeout, so a hanging manager.run_task can block the whole generation despite the timeout constant being defined for evaluation only.

The outer except in evaluate_candidates catches all exceptions from gather but does not set candidate.error for candidates that may have been left unscored by an unexpected exception inside evaluate_single (e.g., an AttributeError in check_import_provenance).

The code sets candidate.score = 0.0 for FileNotFoundError ('pytest not found') and other exceptions, conflating environment failures with test failures; the docstring says 0.0 means 'measured, and bad', but pytest not found is not a measurement.

select_best sorts by score descending but all valid candidates have score exactly 100.0, so the sort is a no-op; the return value is still the first valid candidate, which may not be the 'best' by any other criterion.

The code trusts check_import_provenance to return an object with .ok and .as_error(); if that function raises or returns None, the candidate is left unscored and the outer except logs a generic error.
